passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve.
passages.note: Enacted chapter text of the bill Diaz voted for and co-sponsored; new section 15-2401.01 makes every student eligible to enroll in a public school a qualified student.
Bill overview listing Diaz as a co-sponsor of the same single-subject ESA expansion bill.

rows.reasoning: Diaz co-sponsored and voted Y on HB 2853 (2022), a single-subject Arizona empowerment scholarship account bill whose new section makes a "qualified student" any resident "eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" in preschool-disability, kindergarten or "Any of grades one through twelve" — universal eligibility, which is the rung "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family". The account money pays "Tuition or fees at a qualified school", defined as a "nongovernmental primary or secondary school" with no exclusion of religious schools, so the money follows the student to the family's chosen private or religious school. The first-year appropriation cap does not make this the "most families, not all" rung, because the rungs order eligibility (annex ruling 2026-10-01).
